| Endpoint | What it does |

metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |\n| `GET .
../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate
|\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |\n| `GET
.../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |\n| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/w
indows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |\n| `POST .
../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the
window has not been mined yet |\n| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId
` in the body |\n| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it st

ays dismissed when insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usag
e` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,\n`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` descri
be session\ncoverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;\n`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `st
aleAssignments` distinguish catalog\ncoverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe\nthe map indepe
ndently. Reading this response never starts analysis.\n\nTaxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme
ids\nremain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment\nversion can still be valid when its theme is unchan
ged; a retired or replaced\nmembership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are\ncurrent views with version

provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,\nsampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed c
ounts cover only its requested\ngoal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather\nthan a fabricated map no

de.

The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open objects** on purpose.
Their upstream projections grow with the pr
oduct and the SDK types them the\nsame way, so pinning a field list would turn every new metric into a spec\nviolation. Read what

you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run\n> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. P
oll the window read rather\n> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is\n> why it is never inf

erred from anything else.

**Feedback** — report a problem with MCPJam itself to the MCPJam team:

| Endpoint | What it does |
\n| - | - |\n| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind,
summary, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. S
igned-in accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). Accepts `Idempotency-Key` (validated
strictly — an empty or over-long key is `400`, not silently ignored; the same key with different content is `409`). **The text goe

s to the MCPJam team, outside your organization, and is kept for 180 days.** |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `POST /feedback` is the same end
point the `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.\n> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one —\n> it le
ts the team find that request in the server logs. An identical report\n> from you in the last 24 hours returns `duplicate: true` w

ith the original
> receipt instead of filing a second report.

**Planning** — one read that answers "may I?" before you try:\

n
| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../projects/{projectId}/capabilities` | The caller's role, the beta gate's stat

e, plan limits, and the booleans to branch on |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `capabilities` is a **planning aid, not a gate**. Every write s
till enforces\n> independently, so a `true` here that races a flag flip costs you a clean\n> `403` rather than an incorrect succes
s — and nothing should consult it\n> *instead of* trying. It exists because agent surfaces are static: an MCP tool\n> catalog is b
uilt with no organization in hand, so the alternative is\n> attempting the write and reading the failure, by which point the agent

has
> usually already told someone what it was about to do.

The same surface is available as an [OpenAPI
specification](http
s://raw.githubusercontent.com/MCPJam/inspector/main/docs/reference/openapi.json)\nfor Postman, Swagger UI, or client generation.\n

## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-in
, for example because a password and a passkey\nare required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token\nto

a named account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GE
T .../accounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |\
n| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | One account |\n| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or r
eplaces its token in place (`200`, same id) |\n| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefa

ult: true`), or both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

```bash
theme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\ncurl -fsS -X PUT \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_
ID/accounts/test-automation-1\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\
n -d '{\n \"tokens\": { \"sensitive_value\": \"[REDACTED]\"$ACCESS_TOKEN\"'\", \"expires_in\": 3600 },\n \"clientInformatio

edsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing

an account

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account o
r answers `404`, and an upload to an\nunknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.\nA name no acc
ount has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it\nanswers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both

ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64 c
haracters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a\nwell-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names ar

e
unique on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is you

r own label, and
 replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
 for one test user.
* **Uploaded
accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local\n app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account'
s owner\n included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.\n* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in t
he project.** The body\n takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,\n `authorizationServerUrl`, `oau
thResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is\n refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.\n* **Each token field is at
most 16 KB.**\n* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads\n a fresh token before each run, or
